title: yadgar/project-db
$comment: Closure is per chart (ADR-0850): this file closes only project-db's own key set, at root and in every block it declares; it bounds no other chart. OPEN (untyped {} maps, any shape passes): `global`, the one key the parent forwards into every module; `resources` and `database.instance.resources`, handed to `toYaml` for the pod's and the engine's own resource shape; `rollingUpdate`, handed to `with` for the Deployment's own strategy shape. EXTRAS (a template reads these, `values.yaml` does not declare them, so they are listed as leaves inside their closed block rather than left open): `image.digest`, read by `templates/deployment.yaml` and rewritten with the released digest by ci-release at package time (D65); `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace`, read by `templates/networkpolicy.yaml` (`values.yaml` ships `scrapeFrom: {}`, so without this extra the whole block would stay an open map); `tls.clientAuth`, `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey` (B-U5E expand, folded into C-DB1: the template renders them only when present and the binary is unchanged — B-U5 is what requires them and types `clientAuth`). TYPES, TOGGLES AND `required` ARE A RENDER CHECK'S JOB (ADR-0847), not this file's: `templates/render-checks.yaml` already refuses a non-bool `autoscaling.enabled`, a non-bool `database.create` and a non-map `autoscaling`, by name, and this schema adds nothing on top of those checks. The exceptions. `database.migrationLockTimeoutSeconds` (ledger 814, ADR-0837) keeps its `type: integer, minimum 1, maximum 590`, shipped before ledger 990 and unrelated to it. `database.acquireTimeoutSeconds`, `database.idleTimeoutSeconds`, `database.maxLifetimeSeconds` and `database.engineOperatorReserve` (ledger C-DB2, ADR-0837, ADR-0849) each keep `type: integer, minimum 1`; `acquireTimeoutSeconds` alone also keeps `maximum 29`, pinned below the dial's 30s request deadline by `tests/chart_request_deadline.rs`. `database` keeps `type: object` and `required` naming all five — a required key with a chart default needs no parent-chart or argocd change before a pin (K-8): the module's own `values.yaml` default already satisfies it everywhere, which is why `migrationLockTimeoutSeconds` needed none either. `tls.enabled` (ledger 1278, ADR-0845, C-DB1) keeps `type: boolean` and `tls` keeps `required: [enabled]`: `required` alone passes a null value, so the leaf needs its type too (K-1) — the render check in `templates/render-checks.yaml` still carries the `hasKey`/`kindIs` guard that produces ADR-0845's own sentence, because a schema refusal and a render-check refusal report differently and both are asserted.

migrationLockTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a replica waits for another one's migration before failing its boot. Rendered as DB_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback. Minimum 1: GET_LOCK with 0 never waits and with a negative wait never takes the lock. Maximum 590: see chart/values.yaml.

engineOperatorReserve.description: Connections of engineMaxConnections the pool arithmetic leaves untouched for an operator. Rendered as DB_ENGINE_OPERATOR_RESERVE and read with no fallback (ADR-0837, ADR-0849). Minimum 1: zero leaves a non-admin operator no way into a full engine (store refuses it at connect).

acquireTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds `acquire` waits for a free connection before failing. Rendered as DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837). Minimum 1: zero fails every acquire that has to wait (store refuses it at connect). Maximum 29: strictly below yadgar_dial::default_request_timeout()'s 30s, so this pool's own timeout fires before the caller's whole request deadline does; see chart/values.yaml and tests/chart_request_deadline.rs.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds an idle connection is kept before the pool closes it. Rendered as DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837). Minimum 1: zero churns connections as fast as the pool opens them (store refuses it at connect).

maxLifetimeSeconds.description: Seconds a connection lives before the pool retires it, however busy it is. Rendered as DB_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837). Minimum 1: zero retires a connection before it can do any work (store refuses it at connect).
